title: Principles of microeconomics
audience: a pre-law college student (any major) preparing for law school and the LSAT
purpose: Use supply and demand, elasticity, consumer and producer surplus, costs, market structures, externalities, public goods, information problems and basic game theory.

weeks.10: The Coase theorem and property rights

blocks.deliverable: Find equilibrium price and quantity from equations.
Compute the deadweight loss of a tax.
Find a firm's profit-maximizing output from cost data.
Week 7 midterm; solve a prisoner's dilemma and a monopoly pricing problem.
Explain when bargaining can solve an externality and when it fails.
Explain adverse selection and moral hazard with examples.
Submit the project; take an unseen 120 minute final in week 14.

project: Law-and-economics analysis: pick a legal rule (for example a negligence standard or a noise ordinance), model the incentives it creates with supply-and-demand or game-theory tools, and evaluate it in 1,500 words with numbers.
completion: finish the project, take the week 7 midterm and week 14 cumulative final, then complete a new cumulative assessment after 1 to 2 weeks. Explain one major idea aloud without notes.
